extracted.intended_audience: naval officers, mariners, hydrographic surveyors, and readers of travel/natural-history/exploration accounts
extracted.subtask_description: A 19th-century coastal survey / travel narrative combining hydrographic data, sailing guidance, natural-history observations, and anecdotal reportage for use by mariners and interested readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide precise geographic coordinates and elevations
rubrics_metrics.description: Give latitude and longitude and heights for prominent features and stations (e.g., 'latitude 39 degrees 28 minutes 20 seconds South, and longitude 4 degrees 33 minutes 45 seconds West of Sydney'; summit 1060 feet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes and text routinely record exact positions and elevations for islands, rocks, peaks, and anchorage points to allow charting and cross-checking. Include both main-text references and detailed footnote coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record tidal data with times, ranges, and stream timings/velocities
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify times of high-water at full/change, rise of tide at springs and neaps, start times of flood/ebb streams relative to local high/low water, and velocities in knots (e.g., 'High-water ... 12 hours 5 minutes when the tide rises eight feet; ... northern and ebb stream ... from one to two knots').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide spring/neap distinctions, durations of flood/ebb, slack intervals, and variations between nearby stations (e.g., Preservation Island vs. Swan Island). This technical data is often placed in footnotes for mariner use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe anchorages, depths, and safe passages quantitatively
rubrics_metrics.description: Report depths in fathoms, distance from features, width of channels, and recommended anchorage positions (e.g., 'depth in the middle ... 12 fathoms', 'passage ... six miles wide').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the best anchorage for given wind directions, bottom type (muddy, kelp, rocky), and any restrictions; include distances from shore and notes about shelter or lack of shelter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify hazards and provide leading marks/bearings for pilotage
rubrics_metrics.description: Name reefs, rocks, banks, and give bearings, marks, and instructions to lead safely into inlets (e.g., 'These marks are of use until the eastern and highest of the Direction Isles opens out just clear of the others', 'Mount William bearing South 7 degrees West clears the outer end of it').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give visual leading marks, compass bearings, and distances to avoid specific dangers; specify when particular marks are reliable and any changes with tide or visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use triangulation and astronomical bases in surveying
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish triangulation networks and astronomical base-points for accurate charts (e.g., 'formed an astronomical base for the survey', 'triangulation was extended to Launceston').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe where base stations are placed (summits, lighthouse hills), use multiple angles/observations to fix positions, and note the scale trade-offs when time is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note and analyse local currents and their interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Document flood- and ebb-stream directions, where streams meet, how they neutralize or reinforce each other, and their effect on navigation (e.g., 'The flood-streams setting to the westward through Banks Strait ... meet about ten miles to the westward of the Chappell Isles').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include observations of current strengths, directions, where streams meet to create slack areas, and how wind affects net surface current; quantify velocities where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document flora, fauna and human presence as navigational/contextual notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Record animals, plants, and settlements encountered (e.g., 'fur seals', 'a kind of finch', 'old sealer ... King of the Eastern Straitsmen').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use such natural-history and ethnographic notes to indicate resources (water, fuel), hazards (hosts/hostility), or landing suitability; include abundance, usefulness (e.g., rabbits as food), and behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include human-interest anecdotes and historical extracts to contextualize places
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed stories, personal recollections and historical extracts (e.g., Count Strzelecki's sufferings, log of a hurricane) to enliven the survey narrative and record local history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use narrative anecdotes to explain place names, demonstrate human experience of the area, and provide qualitative information that complements technical data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use footnotes for technical, numerical, and reference information
rubrics_metrics.description: Place dense technical details, precise measurements, timings, and references in footnotes while keeping the main narrative readable (many spots in the text use footnotes to list coordinates, tidal tables, and additional specifics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve main text for descriptive and navigational guidance; relegate long tables, exact coordinates, and publication references to footnotes to avoid interrupting flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical recommendations and policy-level advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Make explicit recommendations about routes, infrastructure, and policy (e.g., 'steamers should at all times use Captain King's inner route', suggestion to establish a coal-depot at Port Essington).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support recommendations with logistical calculations (vessel size, engine horse-power, fuel consumption, distances) and operational reasoning (safety, fuel economy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report vessel maintenance and operational details relevant to voyages
rubrics_metrics.description: Note ship condition and maintenance needs that affect operations (e.g., '130 sheets of copper were required ... two-inch sheathing was completely destroyed').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include descriptions of repairs done, how long they took, and their operational consequences (loss of a tender, time ashore), as these inform future voyage planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ vivid comparative description to situate scenery and mood
rubrics_metrics.description: Use similes and comparisons to familiar regions to convey atmosphere (e.g., 'Such of us as had been in Tierra del Fuego were particularly struck with the resemblance of the scenery in Refuge Cove').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine technical reporting with evocative language to make the account engaging for general readers while preserving usefulness for professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain place-naming and commemorate discoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: Record naming rationale for features (e.g., 'To commemorate my friend Count Strzelecki's discovery ... I called the summit ... Mount Fatigue').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context for names (who/why), especially when names reflect exploration history or honor individuals; this aids future reference and historical record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed meteorological/storm logs with timings and observations
rubrics_metrics.description: When encountering storms, log wind direction changes, timings, barometer status, sea state, sail changes and any losses (e.g., detailed hurricane timeline with times when winds veered, a man washed away, and loss of half-ports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give sequential observations (time-stamped), note instrument failures, visual cues (sky appearance), and manoeuvres taken; these are valuable both as narrative and practical seamanship lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference charts, prior surveys and external publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite earlier charts, surveys and periodicals for corroboration and further information (e.g., 'See Nautical Magazine for December 1845', 'The geological formation ... in Volume 1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sources for claims or extended accounts so readers and mariners can consult original data and cross-check positions and reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise pilotage tactics: approach speeds, use of lights, and use of sheltered inner routes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend operational techniques for safe passage (e.g., 'approaching, at reduced speed, the reefs ... distinguished by means of a powerful light at the vessel's head or bowsprit end', 'steamers ... might effect a saving of fuel as well as time by passing through Torres Strait without anchoring').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain tactical advice with rationale (visibility, current interactions) and practical constraints (wind, engine fuel) so captains can judge applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify geological and topographical features for charting
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and report sizes and shapes of boulders, summits and ridges (e.g., 'a boulder ... measuring eighty feet in height', 'Mount Wilson ... 2350 feet').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide these measurements to help with visual identification from sea and to assist in triangulation and charting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record local settlements, social conditions and security considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe towns, settlements, population character and any lawlessness or danger (e.g., York Town 'almost quite in ruins' and inhabitants a 'lawless set' living by plunder; whaling establishment staffing patterns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include notes useful for landing parties, provisioning, and evaluating risks: availability of supplies, behavior of inhabitants, seasonal occupation patterns.
